text:
Kailer Yamamoto has been one of the quietly best players in Utah this season. Through 16 games he has 12 points, and at five on five the Mammoth take 65% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 10.9 points better than when he's off. That's one of the biggest on-ice edges anywhere.

The goals haven't followed. He's gone nine games without one on 2.7 expected goals, and has three for the season on 5.6 expected. That gap tends to close: he keeps getting the looks. His point rate (2.79 per 60) is running above his talent range, so the assists are carrying him for now. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) puts his primary shot assists at the 84th percentile among forwards. Evolving-Hockey had him 53rd among forwards in wins above replacement last season. He has missed some games, so the season totals undersell him. Our range projects 39 to 60 points if he stays in the lineup.
